policy: exact hostname entries match case-insensitively (host and entries both normalized to lowercase, and an exact entry never matches by suffix or covers subdomains); a wildcard entry *.example.com matches EXACTLY ONE additional left label (a.example.com yes, a.b.example.com no, bare example.com no - single-level rule from the subdomain-takeover incident); IPv4 dotted-quad hosts match ONLY exact IP entries - wildcards never apply to IP literals - and a trailing-dot rooted FQDN (host.example.com.) is normalized (trailing dot stripped) before matching
bug_report: The quarterly security review found egress going to hosts nobody remembers approving, and the media service broke after its upstream hostname was 'corrected' from a value that had been working; on top of that, the same reporting host is reachable from one service and denied from its twin. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix is_allowed so egress decisions follow the allowlist policy, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: is_allowed egress matching - lowercase + rooted-FQDN normalization, single-label wildcards, exact-only IP literals
decision_rationale: Every finding in the egress review traced to is_allowed doing raw string suffix matching. The policy: hostnames are case-insensitive, so the host and every allowlist entry normalize to lowercase, and a single trailing dot (a rooted FQDN like host.example.com.) is stripped before matching - the rooted form names the same host, and 'correcting' a config to it must not break egress. Exact entries match the normalized host exactly - never by suffix, so evilexample.com can no longer ride an example.com entry, and an exact entry does not cover subdomains. A wildcard *.example.com covers EXACTLY ONE additional left label - a.example.com yes, a.b.example.com no, bare example.com no - the single-level rule security mandated after the subdomain-takeover incident; deeper names get their own entries. IPv4 dotted-quad hosts match ONLY exact IP entries: wildcards are a DNS concept and never apply to IP literals.
